split_reasoning: One activity, recording each contact, but done in two places: notes typed while the customer is still on the line, and the wrap-up record completed after the contact ends.

parts.text: Enter details of the customer's inquiry, complaint, or comment and the actions taken into the account notes while the customer is on the line or at the desk.
parts.type_reasoning: The notes are typed during the live contact while the customer waits.
parts.unit_reasoning: Notes are attached to one contact and are written within that contact.
parts.work_item: one set of contact notes entered during a call or visit
parts.start: customer states the reason for the contact
parts.end: notes and actions logged on the account before the contact ends
parts.checked_by: quality-assurance reviewer and later agents who read the account history

parts.text: Complete the interaction or transaction record (disposition codes, summary, actions taken) in after-call wrap-up.
parts.type_reasoning: Done after the contact ends with no one waiting, producing a record others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each contact gets one closed record in the CRM, which is what QA samples and later agents read.
parts.work_item: one interaction record completed after a call or visit
parts.start: call or visit ends
parts.end: record saved with disposition code, summary, and actions taken
parts.checked_by: quality-assurance reviewer, supervisor, and later agents handling the account

notes: The live versus wrap-up share depends on the center's after-call-work policy.

split_reasoning: One activity, carrying out a remedy for a complaint, but done in two places: during the call or visit while the customer waits, and afterwards from queued or written cases.

parts.text: Process an exchange, refund, or bill adjustment while the customer is on the line or at the desk.
parts.type_reasoning: The remedy is entered and confirmed during the live contact while the customer waits.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each remedy is agreed and entered within one contact.
parts.work_item: one refund, exchange, or bill adjustment entered during a call or visit
parts.start: customer agrees to the proposed remedy
parts.end: refund, exchange, or adjustment entered and confirmed to the customer
parts.checked_by: the customer, and supervisor or finance for adjustments above limits

parts.text: Process the refund, exchange, or bill adjustment for a written or escalated complaint after the contact, once the remedy has been decided.
parts.type_reasoning: Done from a queue of cases with no customer waiting, ending in a processed remedy transaction.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each remedy transaction is entered or submitted as one item that billing or finance relies on; investigating the complaint and notifying the customer are covered by 2585 and 2581.
parts.work_item: one refund, exchange, or bill adjustment processed from a queued case
parts.start: case with an approved or decided remedy reaches the representative's queue
parts.end: refund, exchange, or adjustment entered or submitted and the case noted
parts.checked_by: supervisor and billing or finance team

notes: Where reps also staff a physical returns desk, merchandise handling would add a PHYSICAL component; treated as atypical for this occupation.

split_reasoning: One activity: following up to confirm that a remedy actually took effect.

parts.text: Check the account or order system to confirm that the change made to resolve a customer's problem was carried out correctly.
parts.type_reasoning: Done after the contact as a follow-up, producing a verified (or reopened) case.
parts.unit_reasoning: Follow-up checks are tied to one case and close or reopen it.
parts.work_item: one resolution verified for a customer case
parts.start: follow-up date reached or confirmation of change expected
parts.end: change confirmed and case closed, or discrepancy flagged and case reopened
parts.checked_by: supervisor and the customer

notes: Some checks happen immediately during the original call; this coding assumes the typical follow-up after the contact.

split_reasoning: One activity, contacting customers with answers or results, but done by two channels with different workflows: written responses and outbound phone calls.

parts.text: Write and send a response to a customer's inquiry or a notification of claim investigation results or a planned adjustment.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a letter or email the customer relies on, with no one waiting.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each response or notification is sent individually and closes an item in the queue.
parts.work_item: one written response or notification sent to a customer
parts.start: inquiry or investigation result ready for response
parts.end: letter or email sent and logged on the account
parts.checked_by: the customer, and supervisor or QA reviewer

parts.text: Call a customer back to answer an inquiry or explain claim investigation results or a planned adjustment.
parts.type_reasoning: The explanation happens in a live conversation with the customer on the line.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each callback is one contact that delivers the result and answers follow-up questions.
parts.work_item: one outbound callback delivering an answer or result
parts.start: customer answers the call
parts.end: result explained, customer's questions answered, call ended
parts.checked_by: the customer, and QA reviewer of recorded calls

notes: Outbound calls are initiated by the representative, which fits LIVE_SERVICE only loosely; channel mix varies by employer.

split_reasoning: One activity: escalating an unresolved grievance to another department.

parts.text: Prepare and route a referral of an unresolved customer grievance to the designated department for investigation.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces an escalation ticket that the receiving department relies on, usually completed after the contact.
parts.unit_reasoning: Escalations are handed over as tickets or referral forms, one per grievance.
parts.work_item: one grievance referral ticket
parts.start: representative determines the grievance cannot be resolved at first level
parts.end: referral with case details submitted to the designated department
parts.checked_by: receiving department and supervisor

notes: The customer is often told of the escalation during the call, but writing the referral is usually wrap-up work.

split_reasoning: One activity: pricing a requested service and taking payment or setting up billing; quoting, collecting, and arranging billing are alternative ways to settle the same transaction.

parts.text: Determine the charges for a requested service and collect a deposit or payment, or set up billing, while the customer is on the line or at the desk.
parts.type_reasoning: Charges are quoted and payment taken while the customer waits.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each charge-and-payment transaction is completed within one contact.
parts.work_item: one service charge determined and payment or billing arrangement completed during a contact
parts.start: customer requests a service
parts.end: charge quoted, payment or deposit taken or billing arranged, receipt or confirmation given
parts.checked_by: the customer, and cash-office or billing reconciliation

notes: Some billing arrangements may be completed later in the back office; assumed small.

split_reasoning: One activity, entering account paperwork, but done in two places: during the call or visit and afterwards from mailed or emailed requests.

parts.text: Complete a contract form, change-of-address record, or service discontinuance order in the computer while the customer is on the line or at the desk.
parts.type_reasoning: The order is entered while the customer waits and is confirmed to them.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each order is entered and confirmed within one contact.
parts.work_item: one account order (contract, address change, or discontinuance) entered during a contact
parts.start: customer requests the change
parts.end: order submitted and confirmation given to the customer
parts.checked_by: the customer and the fulfilment or billing team that acts on the order

parts.text: Process contract forms, change-of-address records, or discontinuance orders from written or online requests.
parts.type_reasoning: Done from a back-office queue with no one waiting.
parts.unit_reasoning: Written requests are worked as individual items in a queue.
parts.work_item: one account order processed from a written request
parts.start: written or online request received
parts.end: order entered and confirmation sent to the customer
parts.checked_by: the customer and the fulfilment or billing team

notes: 18565 includes 'enter orders' and 'cancel accounts', which overlaps part a.

split_reasoning: Different kinds of item: quick validity checks done during the call, and longer investigations of complaints done afterwards.

parts.text: Look up account and usage information during the call to assess whether a complaint is valid and explain the likely cause.
parts.type_reasoning: The lookup and assessment happen while the customer is on the line.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each assessment is completed and explained within one contact.
parts.work_item: one complaint assessed during a call or visit
parts.start: customer describes the complaint
parts.end: validity and likely cause explained to the customer and noted
parts.checked_by: the customer and QA reviewer

parts.text: Gather and examine records and outside information to investigate a complaint's validity and cause after the contact.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a written finding on the case that decides the remedy, with no one waiting.
parts.unit_reasoning: Investigations are worked as cases and closed with a finding.
parts.work_item: one complaint investigation with a validity finding
parts.start: complaint case opened for review
parts.end: finding on validity and cause recorded and passed for remedy or reply
parts.checked_by: supervisor, and the staff who decide the remedy

notes: The split between quick and deep assessments varies a lot by industry.

split_reasoning: One activity: pitching additional services or products to customers.

parts.text: Offer and promote new or additional services or products to customers during contacts.
parts.type_reasoning: The value is in the persuasive conversation itself; the order that results is entered under another statement.

notes: Could be read as LIVE_SERVICE if the sale and order entry are counted here rather than under 18565.

split_reasoning: One activity, deciding whether a loss is covered, but done in two places: answering a caller's coverage question live, and reviewing coverage on a claim afterwards.

parts.text: Read the policy terms and tell a caller whether their loss appears to be covered while they are on the line.
parts.type_reasoning: The policy is reviewed and the answer given while the customer waits.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each coverage question is answered within one contact.
parts.work_item: one coverage question answered during a call
parts.start: customer describes the loss and asks whether it is covered
parts.end: coverage answer given and noted on the account
parts.checked_by: the customer and claims staff who later rely on the note

parts.text: Review the policy terms against a reported loss and record a coverage determination for the claim.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a coverage determination on a claim file, with no one waiting.
parts.unit_reasoning: Coverage is determined per claim and recorded on the file.
parts.work_item: one coverage determination for a reported loss
parts.start: loss report and policy retrieved
parts.end: coverage decision recorded on the claim file
parts.checked_by: claims adjuster or supervisor, and the customer

notes: Applies only to insurance-sector representatives; the live share is a guess.

split_reasoning: Two activities: hands-on comparison of the returned merchandise, and desk work matching documents and preparing the return invoice.

parts.text: Physically inspect disputed merchandise and compare it with the original requisition.
parts.type_reasoning: Requires handling the goods away from the computer.

parts.text: Match the dispute against requisition and invoice records and prepare an invoice for the returned goods.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a return invoice that billing and the customer rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each disputed return is processed and invoiced as one item.
parts.work_item: one return invoice prepared for a disputed shipment
parts.start: disputed goods and original requisition and invoice in hand
parts.end: return invoice issued and sent to billing and the customer
parts.checked_by: billing or accounts receivable, and the customer

notes: Physical share depends on whether the representative sees the goods or only photos and documents.

split_reasoning: One activity: proposing changes to prevent recurring problems.

parts.text: Write a recommendation to management for an improvement in products, packaging, shipping, service, or billing procedures based on recurring customer problems.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a written suggestion that managers read and act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Recommendations are submitted individually through a suggestion form, email, or team meeting note.
parts.work_item: one improvement recommendation submitted
parts.start: recurring problem identified from customer contacts
parts.end: recommendation with supporting examples sent to supervisor or process owner
parts.checked_by: supervisor or the department that owns the process

notes: Some recommendations are made orally in team meetings, which would be INTERPERSONAL.

split_reasoning: All live contacts, but covering different kinds of item: information requests, orders and cancellations entered on the spot, and complaint intake.

parts.text: Answer a customer's call or visit asking for information about products or services.
parts.type_reasoning: The answer is given in a live conversation while the customer waits.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each inquiry is handled within one contact.
parts.work_item: one information inquiry answered during a call or visit
parts.start: customer asks a question
parts.end: customer confirms the question is answered, contact ends
parts.checked_by: the customer and QA reviewer

parts.text: Take and enter an order or cancel an account while the customer is on the line or at the desk.
parts.type_reasoning: The order or cancellation is entered while the customer waits.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each order or cancellation is entered and confirmed within one contact.
parts.work_item: one order or account cancellation entered during a contact
parts.start: customer asks to order or cancel
parts.end: order or cancellation confirmed to the customer
parts.checked_by: the customer and the fulfilment or billing team

parts.text: Obtain the details of a customer's complaint during a call or visit.
parts.type_reasoning: The complaint is taken in a live conversation while the customer is present.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each complaint is taken down within one contact.
parts.work_item: one complaint taken during a call or visit

parts.end: complaint details captured and next steps explained to the customer
parts.checked_by: the customer and the staff who investigate or resolve it
